rotation.source_passage:
The work of the youngest AEON was flawed,
despite its power: its shining was such that its
own eyes drank the lingering rays, blinding it
to the higher heavens, and thus did the youngest
AEON grow dark, clothed in weight, thinking itself
the first and last. He said in his heart, "I AM.
There is no other besides me."²⁸


He was the youngest and most glorious
of the immovable powers, but his own glory
blinded him to those who came before, and he
was clothed in ignorance, thinking he was the first
and last, the all in all, that there was no other before him.


He lifted up his dark glory, craggy
And jagged with light, and thought in his heart,
"I AM the all in all, there has been no other
Before me, and I am perfect in my oneness. Come,
Let us reproduce our root of oneness, a race
Of subordinates formed from our own substance
That we might see and know our overflowing oneness
And become full with our own bright fullness. Come"²⁹
rotation.underlying_attribution: §V. Kanye Creates the Material Cosmos by Mistake
rotation.enantiomorph:
The work of the youngest AEON was sound,
despite its power: its shining was such that its
own eyes passed the lingering rays, clarifying it
to the higher heavens, and thus did the youngest
AEON grow still, clothed in lightness, knowing itself
the latest and least. He was silent in his heart.
²⁸


He was the youngest and most transparent
of the immovable powers, but his own transparency
opened him to those who came before, and he
was clothed in recollection, knowing he was the latest
and least, a thread among threads, that there were all others before him.


He set down his quiet clarity, smooth
And continuous with light, and knew in his heart,
he was a thread among threads, there had been all others
Before him, and he was partial in my portion.
Let us attend our root of descent, a chorus
Of elders received from beyond our substance
That we might see and know our overflowing indebtedness
And become full with our own bright incompleteness.²⁹

independent_verification.recovered_law: In Text A, the youngest AEON's own glory blinds it to what came before, causing it to falsely declare itself the sole, self-sufficient origin and to generate subordinates from its own substance; in Text B, the youngest AEON's transparency opens it to what came before, causing it to recognize itself as derivative and indebted, attending to elders received from beyond its own substance. The direction of self-relation is reversed: from self-enclosed originary sovereignty to receptive acknowledgment of prior others.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural reversal: the youngest power's glory shifts from blinding/self-enclosed (causing false claims of sole primacy and generating subordinates) to transparent/receptive (revealing what preceded it, with no claim of solitary primacy).
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final portion of Text B consistently maintains the reversed relation — the AEON remains derivative, partial, and indebted rather than reverting to self-originating sovereignty.
